priorities.name: Enclosed space for focus and discretion
priorities.issue: Even as the top-ranked site, Atlanta's most-cited gap is too few capsules/rooms for discreet meetings and phone calls taken in hallways carrying noise.
whatItLooksLike: The limited number of capsules to have meetings that require discretion. The limitation of 2 hours in each capsule.
Some locations can be too noisy because people tend to take phone calls in the hallway areas.

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (74/100).
Noise & Distraction: 58 comments (52% neg); Privacy & Confidentiality: 57 comments (49% neg).
Focused-space friction 23/100 (46% under-supported); the 2-hour capsule limit is called out.

priorities.proposedAction: Review capsule/room booking rules (including the 2-hour cap) and a hallway-calls etiquette nudge before adding rooms.
priorities.siteMustDo: Test whether relaxing/adjusting the capsule time limit and a hallway-call norm reduce the complaints; measure before/after.

priorities.name: Workstation hardware standardization
priorities.issue: Monitors are reset to unusable positions each visit and shared keyboards/mice are a hygiene concern, adding friction to every arrival.
whatItLooksLike: Hinder = 1) Monitors are unnecessarily 'reset' to locations that are unusable and each visit requires maneuvering monitors/cords/etc. 2) Keyboards/mice - We went from Covid is the plague to communal keyboards/mice. I'm the furthest thing…

evidence.text: Hardware: 55 comments, 47% negative. Connectivity: 31 comments, 52% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Standardize monitor/dock setup, run routine checks, and address the shared-peripheral hygiene concern (wipes or personal-kit option).
priorities.siteMustDo: Inspect stations, fix the monitor-reset issue, and provide a hygiene option for shared peripherals.

priorities.name: Thermal comfort (temperature)
priorities.issue: Temperature is a specific, negative complaint concentrated in certain zones.
whatItLooksLike: Temperature is called out as too cold in several comments (see Physical Feature detail).

evidence.text: Temperature / Thermal: 30 comments, 57% negative; thermal friction 16/100 (37% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Check HVAC set-points/balancing in the flagged zones; confirm a durable fix.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log the cold zones/times and verify the correction holds.

priorities.name: Reserved-desk etiquette and visibility
priorities.issue: Associates arrive to find someone in the desk or room they reserved, with nothing at the desk showing it is reserved, and some people hold more than one space at a time.
whatItLooksLike: Its frustrating when another Elevance employee decides to sit in the space that I reserved for the day.
When someone sits down at a station that is reserved, there is no indication. It would be helpful to discourage them from using what's been reserved.
Other associates taking up multiple spaces by reserving more than one space ( focus room and work station) at the same time. …

evidence.text: Desk Availability & Reservations: 98 comments, 45% negative — the highest-volume theme at the site not already covered by P1–P3.
'Reservation tools are easy to use' agreement: 4.23 vs 4.03 company average (Strong).
The tool itself rates well, so the fix is behavior and visibility — who is sitting in a reserved seat — not a new system.

priorities.proposedAction: Make reserved status visible at the desk (check-in, or a reserved indicator if the system supports it), auto-release unclaimed bookings, and set a one-space-at-a-time norm.
priorities.siteMustDo: Spot-check reserved vs. occupied desks on peak days, confirm which check-in/indicator features exist, and communicate the etiquette norm.

priorities.name: Chair condition and adjustability
priorities.issue: Worn chairs with failing adjustments and torn arm pads mean associates try several desks before they can settle — a condition problem at specific desks rather than a site-wide furniture gap.
whatItLooksLike: I seem to have bad luck with selecting workstations whose chairs are wobbly and worn out. Usually it takes a few desks before I find one that has working adjustments and isn't falling apart even if it looks ok from the outside.
Many chair arm pads are ripped on Quad B 12th floor and need to be repaired.
Chairs and tables are old. More than 5+ years

evidence.text: Furniture comfort & ergonomics: on Target — friction 10/100 (28% under-supported).
The survey item is on Target, so treat this as repairing and replacing worn chairs, not a furniture refresh.

priorities.proposedAction: Have Workplace Operations audit chair condition floor by floor, repair or replace failed chairs (starting with Quad B, 12th floor), and add a simple way to tag a broken chair.
priorities.siteMustDo: Complete the chair audit, take failing chairs out of service, and confirm repairs or replacements within 30 days.

protectWhatIsWorking.evidence: highest of all sites (82.5/100) — the whole service experience is a model to protect
